notes:
- The fiber distribution unit check now follows how FDUs are really placed: an FDU nested under the PLC, RIO, or patch panel it belongs to (same UPN) needs no dependency, and one that names that equipment as a dependency is fine too. Only an FDU hanging off a header alone, with nothing listed, is flagged
- The rule text and its worked example no longer suggest an FDU should list the equipment it serves — a dependency is what a row relies on, and the equipment an FDU serves is either above it in the tree or lists the FDU itself

- The loading circle spins again — and the arc now keeps up with the number: previously the arc eased so slowly that it could still show around 20% while the label already read 45%. The section you see always matches the percentage

- The loading circle is now a true gauge: the arc starts at the top, stays put, and its length always matches the number — 45% shows 45% of the circle
- Progress is reported step by step: importing shows opening, scanning, parsing, and checking as separate stages, and exporting names each part of the workbook as it is compressed, so the percentage moves smoothly instead of jumping
- On a large registry the one unavoidable pause (writing the workbook itself) is labelled before it starts, and the loader keeps breathing through it

- Visual pass across every screen at desktop, tablet, and narrow widths:
- Fixed the finding boxes clipping in the SSM Hierarchy equipment drawer (the level chip was squeezed into a column narrower than the chip)
- Sidebar counts now show compactly from four digits up (7.1k, 23k — exact number in the tooltip), so the Audit Findings label never gets cut to "…"
- Fixed level chips being trimmed in the Checks overview table on narrow windows
- The worked-example table in Rules keeps a visible scrollbar so it is obvious there is more to the right

- Fixed Show in hierarchy not visibly highlighting the target: the jump scrolled the tree before its rows existed, so the scroll was clamped to the top and the highlight happened off screen unless the equipment sat in the first viewport. The tree now renders, then scrolls, then draws the window around the target — the row lands centred and pulses
- Jumping again within a few seconds no longer cuts the new highlight short

- UPN SEC is now recognised as belonging to Security: rows with System Name "Security" or "Security Systems" on UPN SEC pass the System-Name check
- UPN MISC is treated as the catch-all it is: MISC rows no longer get the impossible System-Name error — instead every MISC row carries a Note reminding you to double-check whether an approved UPN fits, and the new check has its own worked example on the Rules screen

- UPN RR is now recognised as belonging to the CSA system: rows with System Name "CSA" or "Civil Structural Architectural Systems (CSA)" on UPN RR pass the System-Name check instead of being flagged Invalid
- CSA on a numeric UPN, or a numeric system on RR, still flags as before

- Show in hierarchy now lands with a clear temporary highlight: the equipment row pulses orange for about three seconds after the jump, then settles back
- Menu and page titles read Audit Findings, SSM Hierarchy, and Compare Projects

- Fixed the findings list sometimes going blank below halfway: grouped section headers were shorter than the list's fixed row height, so the rendered slice fell short of the screen
- Fixed level counts clipping on the Dashboard's milestone readiness table when numbers pass three digits: the By level column is wider and wraps instead of cutting off
- The Dashboard's deep-dive sections (Milestone readiness, Hierarchy health, Dependencies, Checks overview, Structure) now share one tab strip, so the page is one screen tall instead of a long scroll

- Equipment with several findings is now one merged block in the report: the equipment appears once, its findings stack beside it, and a single Actioned box covers the whole block (ticking it turns the entire block green)
- New report layout option in the export chooser: one tab per finding level (Invalid / Rule broken / Check this / Note) instead of one per milestone — flagged equipment only, ordered by milestone, with an L2 Milestone column; the Dashboard and Index follow whichever layout is chosen

- Export now opens a chooser first: for each finding level — or any individual check — pick Include, Pre-ticked, or Leave out
- Pre-ticked findings arrive with the Actioned box already ☑ (green row, counted as done); Leave out findings are not written into the report at all, and every count and progress bar reflects it
- An equipment row only starts ticked when every one of its findings is pre-ticked; the equipment tree itself is always complete
- Your choices are remembered for the next export of the same session

- The Excel report is now about a quarter of the size (a 20,000-row registry drops from roughly 24 MB to 6 MB): the workbook is zipped with a proper compressor and repeated finding text is stored once
- Fixed Excel asking to repair large reports: per-discipline progress is now calculated on a hidden Calc sheet instead of one very long formula that exceeded Excel's limit on registries with many milestones
- The export shows a progress overlay while it builds

- Fixed the update download: GitHub changed where release files are served from, which blocked the in-app fetch. The Download button now hands the file straight to the browser, so it lands in Downloads as SSM-Audit-v<version>.html

- Every check on the Rules screen now has an Example button: a small made-up registry that shows exactly what gets flagged, with the cell shaded and the offending characters marked, alongside why it is flagged, what the audit says about it, and what right looks like
- Each example is run through the real audit engine when opened, so the verdict shown is live, not a copy

- Excel report Dashboard redesigned: a large overall progress bar at the top, the level totals, and wide progress bars with live percentages per discipline and per L2 phase (the Index keeps its compact form)
- Actioned is now a tick box: click the cell and choose ☑; the row turns green and every progress figure updates
- Milestone tabs: each nest level has its own colour (not shades of one), equipment IDs are always black, Dependencies sits right after Closest Parent, Building and Item Master are included, and the cell a finding is about (UPN, Closest Parent, Dependencies, System Name, …) is shaded light red

- The update check is no longer silent: the Changelog window now says whether you are on the latest version, whether a newer one is available, or why the check could not run, with a Check again button
- When GitHub limits checks from a busy network (60 an hour per site address), SSM Audit falls back to a second source so the update still shows
- The automatic check quietly retries once if the first attempt runs before the network is ready
- Tightened every transition so the app feels snappy as well as smooth: panels open in 180ms and close in 110ms, control feedback is 120ms, and screen changes settle in 160ms

- Full UI motion pass: the Guide, update window, finding drawer, Filters panel, and progress overlay now ease in and ease out (backdrop fade, panel slide or scale) instead of snapping
- Switching screens slides the new content in; buttons, chips, tiles, tabs, tree toggles, and table rows share one consistent hover and press feel
- Everything respects the operating system's reduced-motion setting

- Fixed the menu overlapping itself on narrow windows: the top bar now scrolls when its items do not fit, drops to icons under 640px, and the version badge moves into the top bar instead of floating over content

- Replaced the row of filter dropdowns with one Filters panel covering level, discipline, L2 milestone, UPN, building, source, topic, and individual checks; only the active filters show on the page, as removable chips
- The Dashboard now scopes to the same filters, so it can be narrowed to one building, discipline, or phase, and it gained milestone readiness per L2 phase, hierarchy health, a dependencies view, a checks overview that also shows which checks passed, and an Item Master migration gauge

- Added filters by discipline, L2 milestone, UPN, and building on Audit findings, with a chip per active selection — deselect a discipline to set it aside, for example hide Electrical to see which other disciplines list a parent as a dependency
- Added checks found by auditing real registries: a parent in another building, a dependency pointing at an organizational header, a parent duplicated as a dependency (noted, since electrical does this routinely), a system with no row at its top, an Equipment ID that reads like a typed description, Dependency Project filled although every dependency is local, and a note on classifications not in the Rev21 dropdown so site-specific codes can be reviewed
- Driven and control equipment now count as powered when their parent carries the electrical feed, removing false alarms on fan filter units and similar equipment
- An instrument whose tag names a different UPN than its row is now a note when the row and its parent agree — a tag question rather than a nesting error
- Dashboard gained tiles for site-specific classifications and parent-as-dependency counts

- Added a Dashboard, the first item in the menu and the screen an audit opens on: totals by level, where the problems are by discipline, system, and L2 phase, the checks firing most, and the shape of the registry — every number opens the findings narrowed to it, with a clearable filter chip
- Renamed the four finding levels again to fit already-uploaded registries: Invalid, Rule broken, Check this, and Note
- Updated the guide, report headings, and README to match

- Added a relationship diagram to each parent, dependency, and loop finding that labels which tag is this equipment, which is its parent or dependency, and the order of a loop
- Renamed the four finding levels to say what they mean: Won't upload, Breaks a rule, Check this, and Note
- Rewrote the in-app guide and README to match the current workspace, checks, and report

- Item Master checks now recognize any site-prefixed name (not only CA_) and propose the VF equivalent; a registry that is wholesale on a site scheme is reported as a migration note per row rather than thousands of warnings
- Fixed wording in header findings

- Added a professional Excel report: a dashboard with progress bars, a hyperlinked index, one tab per L2 phase with nesting levels and an Actioned column that updates the totals as you work, plus every finding and every check
- Rewrote every check and every finding in plain language so anyone can read why a row was flagged and what to do
- Aligned checks with the approved Rev21 upload lists and the SSM SOP: UPNs and System Names are checked against the approved values, headers are recognized by their Blank Item Master, and new SOP checks cover instruments, VFDs, local control panels, control valves, and room sensors
- Redesigned the workspace: a left sidebar to move between findings, hierarchy, comparison, and rules; a wider table with the reason as the headline; a richer detail panel with Show in hierarchy; grouping by check or phase; and a Findings-only view in the hierarchy
- Improved the hierarchy explorer with finding counts on every branch and header rows shown distinctly

- Fixed registry imports with the updated spreadsheet reader
- Fixed project comparisons so changed parent placement and hierarchy cycles cannot appear aligned
- Fixed hierarchy grouping, external relationship handling, and duplicate-sheet imports
- Improved large-registry performance, iPad comparison layouts, accessibility, and audit exports

- Added full-height Hierarchy, System Differences, and Equipment Mapping tabs inside Project Comparison
- Improved electrical and FMS alignment across site naming differences using equipment meaning, neutral tag identity, and hierarchy context
- Improved comparison navigation so searches, branch expansion, and scroll state remain available while switching views
- Added every system observation to the in-app differences view and refined responsive layouts for desktop and iPad

- Added an interactive SSM Hierarchy tab for exploring one registry from Building through Discipline, System Name, and Equipment
- Added fast hierarchy search, cascading filters, expand and collapse controls, fullscreen review, and persistent tree state
- Added equipment details showing metadata, closest parent, dependencies, source row, and related audit findings
- Optimized large hierarchy rendering and responsive layouts for desktop, iPad, and narrow screens

- Added a synchronized side-by-side project comparison for reviewing system hierarchy, headers, dependencies, and I&C placement by UPN
- Added a searchable, plain-language Rules workspace showing every check currently used by the audit
- Improved registry and commissioning findings with clearer evidence, filtering, sorting, and report exports
- Improved large-registry performance and responsive layouts for desktop and iPad

- Refocused completed-registry audits on internal integrity, SSM SOP conformance, and commissioning logic instead of pre-upload completeness or broad dropdown vocabulary
- Added confidence-rated checks for RIO controller paths, VFD and starter placement, heat-trace chains, fiber distribution dependencies, and VESDA fire-alarm dependencies
- Improved header detection, three- and four-digit UPN validation, rule confidence visibility, and audit report coverage
- Fixed commissioning-path checks so organizational VF_Blank headers are not audited as physical equipment

- Added multi-select filters for rule source, severity, category, and individual rules, plus Excel-style sorting
- Added commissioning checks for missing electrical enabling paths, control power paths, and control-system links
- Improved audit language so findings cite concise Cx Upload Validation, SSM SOP, or Commissioning Logic rules without naming source workbooks
- Added the complete rule catalog to the Guide and exported audit reports

- Added a standalone SSM Audit for checking completed Cx Registries against the SSM SOP and approved Exto Rev21 values
- Added evidence, expected results, recommended corrections, and accurate physical Excel row references for every finding
- Added cached filtering, fullscreen review, deep-hierarchy protection, and downloadable Excel audit reports
- Kept audit workbooks local, temporary, and completely separate from hierarchy learning
